C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL.Name: Mini-git document change journal: a UI-free renderer library that records who/what/when for every change to an open document (in-app edits, external writes, system rewrites), computes two-level diffs between any two recorded states on the existing diff-match-patch engine, and exposes a query API — the shared foundation for agent-edit visibility, conflict handling, review and file recovery

C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL.Summary: Four planned features need the same three answers about an open document — who changed it, what changed, and when — and today Mark has only a fragment of the machinery: a per-tab ring of five pre-reload snapshots (store/diffSnapshots.js) feeding one manual diff view, written at two call sites inside the live-reload path. The 2026-10-23 code read also confirmed a live defect in that path: with liveReload ON (the default), an external write silently REPLACES a dirty tab's buffer (editor.js:2212 — the condition `isSaved || liveReload || ...` bypasses the conflict banner whenever liveReload is on); the unsaved text survives only inside the snapshot ring. This change builds the shared foundation as a UI-free renderer library: an append-only per-document journal of ChangeRecords {stateRef, timestamp, actor{kind}, trigger} with triggers for in-app edit pauses, external write batches (consumed from the existing watcher pipeline, not replacing it), and system rewrites; a two-level diff API (coarse muya-block hunks plus fine line/word detail inside changed blocks) built on the existing diff-match-patch dependency; kind-level attribution (user / external / system) with the actor model reserving label+confidence fields for later identity attribution; and an explicit external-write batch policy (minimum quiet gap plus a forced cut under continuous writes, with atomic rename-writes as the clean single-event case). store/diffSnapshots.js becomes a thin consumer of the journal while keeping its public call shape and ring semantics, so the existing diff view and its tests stay green. The library ships with no UI, no disk writes, and no Rust changes; every consumer surface (agent-edit visibility flash/rail, conflict merge UI, review accept/reject, file history) is a separate change bundle reading this API.

Problem.Description: Mark's agent-era roadmap has four consumers that all need per-document change history: (1) the agent-edits-visible feature (backlog, 2026-10-23) must know which regions an external writer changed and when; (2) the dirty-tab + external-write conflict path must be able to compare base/mine/theirs — and the 2026-10-23 code read proved that path is defective TODAY: with liveReload ON (default, preferences.js:149) an external write overwrites a dirty buffer silently (editor.js:2205-2270: the reload branch runs whenever `isSaved || liveReload || readOnlyReload || tab.watchMode` holds, so liveReload alone forces the swap on an unsaved tab; only the snapshot ring preserves the lost text); (3) the review/tracked-changes item (2026-10-19) needs stable document states to accept/reject against; (4) local file recovery (the 2026-10-18 Obsidian-audit candidate) needs "what did this document look like N minutes ago". Today the only shared asset is store/diffSnapshots.js — a ring of five snapshots recorded opportunistically before live reloads, consumed by one manual diff view, with no attribution, no in-app-edit records, no query API, and no batch boundary definition. Each consumer building its own history would duplicate the same machinery four times with divergent semantics. The owner's direction (2026-10-23) names the shape: a universal object/function module — a mini-git without git — that answers who/what/when once, for everyone.

Goals.R-1: Journal (ledger): an append-only, session-scoped, in-memory journal per open document. Each ChangeRecord carries {stateRef (full-content snapshot reference), timestamp, actor{kind, label?, confidence?}, trigger, stats{lines, bytes}}. Triggers recorded: in-app edit (coalesced on typing pause), external write batch (arriving through the existing watcher pipeline), system rewrite (formatter or equivalent whole-document transformation). Untitled tabs without a pathname are not journaled (same rule as today's snapshots).
Goals.R-2: Two-level diff API: a pure, deterministic diff(stateA, stateB) returning hunks at two granularities — coarse hunks keyed by content-derived block anchors (heading path, ordinal and block type computed from the markdown of each state — never the transient muya ag-N keys, which are minted per parse and are not stored with a state), plus fine line/word detail inside each changed block — built on the existing diff-match-patch dependency (^1.0.5, package.json:58); no new diff library is introduced. Identical inputs produce identical output (snapshot-testable).
Goals.R-3: Attribution model, kind level only in v1: actor.kind is one of user (change made inside this Mark), external (change arrived from disk), system (Mark-applied whole-document transformation). The record shape reserves optional label and confidence fields, but nothing in this change populates identity: process heuristics (lsof "probable: node/ZCode/claude") and announced channels (mark CLI marker) are deferred, and any UI built on the journal must render kind-level truth only ("external change", never "changed by agent X").
Goals.R-4: External-write batch policy, defined and implemented once in the journal: a batch closes on a minimum quiet gap after the last watcher event, OR is force-cut after a bounded window of continuous writes (so a writer emitting events every ~150 ms still yields discrete batches), with atomic rename-writes treated as the clean single-event case. The policy consumes the existing Rust watcher events (m013b, 200 ms debounce) and the existing renderer settle (100 ms) plus hash-skip; it does not modify the Rust watcher.
Goals.R-5: Snapshot-ring migration: store/diffSnapshots.js becomes a thin consumer of the journal (the journal is the single recorder of document states). All six diffSnapshots call sites keep their shape: four recordSnapshot calls in editor.js (the data and disk branches of BLOCK_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE_RELOAD_DATA plus the two CONFIRM_* branches) and the two recordOpenedSnapshot calls (the opened baseline and the session-restore path). Both structures the diff view consumes are preserved: the five-entry ring behind latestSnapshot and the replaceable C-68 opened slot behind openedSnapshot. The diff view keeps working unchanged, and the opened-baseline e2e plus every existing diffSnapshots suite stay green.
Goals.R-6: Performance gate: recording a batch and computing its diff must stay off the critical rendering path — a 10k-line document fixture is pinned in tests with an explicit time budget (number set at plan time from measured baseline), and the reload path's existing behavior (scroll clamp, cursor preservation, 650a555f stale-block drop) is unchanged.
Goals.R-7: The module ships UI-free and renderer-side: no Vue components, no new store actions beyond the library's own API, no new Tauri/Rust commands, no IPC. MODULE_CONTRACT with ROLE appropriate for a library module; consumers render, the journal computes.

Constraints.Item: Nothing is written into .md files, the repository, or any watched/synced folder by this change; the journal is session memory only (cross-session persistence and its storage format are a separate future change with the storage/privacy rules already recorded in the backlog entry).

The existing watcher pipeline is consumed, not replaced: m013b/watch.rs, the renderer watch facade, the 200 ms Rust debounce, the 100 ms settle and the hash-skip stay as they are; the batch policy lives renderer-side in the journal.
diff-match-patch remains the diff engine; no new diff dependency is added.
The existing diff view (components/editorWithTabs/diffView.vue) keeps its behavior and tests; migration must be invisible to it beyond the recording source.

The live-reload behavior chain is untouched by this change: loadChange, scroll clamping (81213fe0), stale-block drop (650a555f) and the dirty-tab paths behave exactly as before — including the live defect described in the Problem; repairing it is explicitly out of scope (see NonGoals) so that the repair is not gated on this module.
Attribution honesty is normative: kind-level truth only; label/confidence fields exist in the model but no code path populates them in this change; consumer UI wording must not claim authorship.
All governed edits ship MODULE_CONTRACT / MODULE_MAP / CHANGE_SUMMARY updates; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; graph and verification deltas land in the same bundle as the code.
English repo artifacts; the owner's Russian direction is quoted in translation with the original preserved in the backlog entry.

Memory bound: the journal keeps at most 50 records or 8 MiB per open document, whichever comes first, evicting the oldest record first; the journal is cleared when the tab closes (the clearSnapshots precedent). The plan pins a retained-memory assertion with that number so retention is not left to "as specified at plan time".
Diagnostics stay content-free: journal logs and error reports carry {tabId, trigger, stats} only — never document text, diff bodies or pathnames; the journal is in-memory and dies with the tab.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Repairing the dirty+liveReload silent overwrite (live defect in APPLY_FILE_CHANGE, editor.js ~2416-2573): recommended as its own small fix bundle so it can ship fast without waiting for this module — routing a dirty tab at external write into the existing conflict banner instead of the silent swap. The owner's decision on bundling (separate fix vs fold into this change) is the flagged open fork; as drafted, this spec does not repair it.
Three-way merge (base/mine/theirs) and any conflict-resolution UI — the follow-up change that both consumes this journal and resolves the conflict path properly.
Identity attribution (lsof process heuristics, mark CLI announcement channel) — deferred with the model fields reserved.
Disk persistence, cross-session retention, and history for closed files or non-open workspace files — v3 territory per the backlog entry.

Any user-facing surface: agent-visibility flash/rail/follow (separate backlog item and future bundle), review accept/reject, history UI, notification cards (the C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM source enum already reserves an 'agent' channel; wiring it is that system's future, not this library's).
Tracked-changes review records inside documents (the 2026-10-19 item) — boundary: the journal is local metadata and never enters the file; review records are document content.
Version-control features: branches, commits, user-visible history browsing, .git directories, any git interoperability.
Rust-side journal storage or new backend commands.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Journal unit suite: every trigger kind (in-app pause, external batch, system rewrite) produces a ChangeRecord with correct actor.kind, monotonic timestamps and stats; append-only semantics hold; untitled tabs record nothing; the 50-record / 8 MiB bound holds and the oldest record is evicted first.

Two-level diff fixtures (EN+RU markdown: headings, lists, task lists, tables, code fences, footnotes): coarse hunks map to the expected muya block keys and fine detail covers line and word changes; identical inputs yield identical output across runs.

Batch policy tests with synthetic watcher-event streams: a minimum quiet gap closes a batch; a continuous ~150 ms event stream is force-cut into discrete batches within the bounded window; an atomic rename-write yields exactly one batch; the hash-skip (disk content equals tab content) records nothing.

Snapshot-ring migration: the four recordSnapshot sites and the two recordOpenedSnapshot sites in editor.js keep their call shape; the diff view opens and renders both the latest ring state and the replaceable opened baseline as before; all existing diff-view, opened-snapshot and live-reload specs stay green, including tests/e2e/diff-opened-baseline.spec.ts and tests/e2e/live-reload-scroll.spec.ts.

Performance gate: the 10k-line fixture records a batch and computes its two-level diff within the plan-time budget on the test runner; the live-reload scroll-clamp e2e stays green and the V-M-025 open-file-timing budget is unchanged.
No UI and no backend: grep-pinned absence of new Vue components or Tauri commands introduced by this change; the library is importable and testable headlessly (vitest).

Attribution shape: actor model carries label/confidence fields but no production path sets them; a unit test pins that every ChangeRecord carries actor = {kind} with one of the three values, and a source assertion pins that no production path writes label or confidence.

npm test green; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; .grace/graph (new library module entry plus updated diffSnapshots/editor edges) and .grace/verification (journal, diff, batch-policy suites) updated in the same bundle.

AffectedAreas.Item: src/renderer/src/store/diffSnapshots.js — becomes a thin consumer of the journal; public call shape and ring semantics preserved; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP updated.
src/renderer/src/store/editor.js — the four recordSnapshot sites and the two recordOpenedSnapshot sites keep their shape; consumption wiring only; CHANGE_SUMMARY updated.

NEW renderer library module (candidate location src/renderer/src/documentHistory/ — final location at plan time): journal, two-level diff, batch policy, actor model; MODULE_CONTRACT with ROLE: RUNTIME (the word "library" belongs in PURPOSE; the protocol role enum is RUNTIME | TEST | BARREL | CONFIG | TYPES | SCRIPT).
tests/renderer/ — new unit suites for journal, diff fixtures, batch policy, migration; performance fixture.
.grace/graph/ + .grace/verification/ — module and suite entries in the same bundle.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx vitest run tests/renderer/document-history/ && npm test
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit suites green for journal records, two-level diff fixtures (EN+RU), batch-policy event streams and the snapshot-ring migration; existing diff-view and live-reload specs unchanged and green; performance fixture within the plan-time budget; grace lint --assertions current = 0 with graph/verification deltas in the bundle. Pre-implementation active-baseline check: run grace lint on main before starting; this evidence is the change's own gate, not a final-state claim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The dirty+liveReload silent-swap reading of editor.js:2205-2270 (2026-10-23 code read) is accurate: the reload branch runs for a dirty tab whenever liveReload is ON, with recordSnapshot preserving the pre-swap buffer. The repair fork assumes a separate fix bundle unless the owner folds it in at approval.
diff-match-patch is sufficient for fine-grained markdown diffs at document sizes Mark handles (tens of thousands of lines worst case); the performance gate exists to falsify this cheaply if wrong.
muya block keys are accessible from the renderer store layer at recording time (they already flow through tab state); exact access is a plan-time detail.
Session-scoped memory is acceptable for every v1 consumer (agent-visibility v2 "since last viewed" works within a session; recovery-across-relaunch is explicitly v3).
